title: Make CLI credential entry safe by default
lead: Reduce accidental passphrase exposure in CLI use. Keep environment, file, and stdin inputs available; decide whether the inline `--passphrase` option should be removed or explicitly deprecated, and document the resulting workflow.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The CLI accepts --passphrase, which can expose the secret in process listings. Environment, file, and stdin inputs already exist and the documentation recommends them.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; README.md; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md; scripts/test-local.sh (CI smoke script used inline --passphrase).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Add CLI coverage that environment, passphrase-file, and passphrase-stdin inputs continue to work. Add a case proving inline --passphrase is rejected and does not echo a supplied secret.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Remove the CLI --passphrase option and its resolver branch; retain the library Passphrase API. Keep environment, file, and stdin mechanisms. Update usage text and docs to direct users to those inputs.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Run focused CLI credential tests and the full solution test suite. Check help output and all docs for stale inline-passphrase examples.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Do not include real passphrases in tests, fixtures, output, or commit messages.
